profile_text.body:
Arm is a public company founded in 1990 and headquartered in Cambridge, United Kingdom. According to its website, Arm provides compute platforms for AI across cloud, edge, and physical systems, describing itself as delivering "the compute platforms behind today's most advanced AI, trusted by innovators worldwide." The company positions its Arm compute platform as connecting cloud, edge, and physical AI with consistent software and flexible compute.

Arm's AI offerings include the Arm AI Portal, which the company describes as giving developers and agents one place to discover optimized models, evaluate performance, access deployment workflows, and optimize models for Arm. The site also highlights the AGI CPU, presented as part of how Arm supports agentic AI in data centers. Arm emphasizes applications ranging from edge AI on consumer and embedded devices, which it says must run with instant response, reliability, and strict power limits, to autonomous machines and AI-defined vehicles requiring real-time compute within power and safety constraints. The company also mentions NVIDIA DGX Spark, built on Arm-based NVIDIA Grace Blackwell technology, as enabling developers to develop, fine-tune, and run large AI models locally.
